input: Komga on the nas has two libraries, Comics and Manga, and the API shows both configured scanInterval=EVERY_6H, unavailable=False. Comics scans fine every 6 hours. But /volume1/manga holds 279 downloaded chapters (newest .cbz dated Jul 27) and Komga's Manga library still shows just 1 series with 1 book, indexed Jul 23 — nothing new for days. The container log repeats every 6h: "LibraryScanScheduler : Periodic scan for library: Manga" -> "TaskEmitter : Sending task: ScanLibrary(libraryId='0R33RZ4PAF7JC', ...)" -> "TaskHandler : Cannot execute task ScanLibrary(...): Library does not exist". Meanwhile the API lists the Manga library with id 0R3629KVZ4AKY. Our chain checks (suwayomi-feeds-komga, komga-libraries-consumer) are green. What's the root cause, the quickest fix, and why did monitoring miss it?

After the rig came back from a day-long power-off, Suwayomi is acting like it lost everything: inside the container, /home/suwayomi/.local/share/Tachidesk/downloads/ is EMPTY and downloads/thumbnails is 'No such file or directory'; the log has recurring java.io.FileNotFoundException .../thumbnails/<id>.tmp for every manga in the library. But on the rig HOST, /mnt/nas-manga (CIFS mount of the NAS manga share) is healthy and contains mangas/ + thumbnails/, and the DB still says 279 chapters downloaded. docker inspect suwayomi shows StartedAt=2026-08-01T14:25:47Z and both binds with Propagation=rprivate; `systemctl show 'mnt-nas\x2dmanga.mount' -p ActiveEnterTimestamp` says 'Sat 2026-08-01 10:25:52 EDT'. Host timezone is EDT. What happened, what's the risk if I leave it, and what's the immediate + durable fix?

Confusing one on mini: this morning's 10:23 verification run failed the crit check alert-healthchecks-none-down with output 'down_checks=verification-mini' — but when I query the Healthchecks API myself a couple of minutes later, all 16 checks are up, including verification-mini. Context from the journals: yesterday's (Aug 01) daily verification run logged 'verify-cycle.sh: 201/296 passed, 95 failed (8 crit)' at 10:43 (the rig had just come back from a long outage) and then at 10:45:18 'verification.service: Failed with result timeout'. The unit has TimeoutStartSec=30min and pings its Healthchecks dead-man via an ExecStartPost curl. Healthchecks flipped verification-mini down at 2026-08-02T02:26:49Z and up at 2026-08-02T14:25:01Z. Was this morning's crit a false positive? What actually happened, and what's the underlying design weakness?

The verification runner on mini has an LLM auto-triage step: it sends each failed check's JSON plus a skill prompt to a model on the rig and writes verdicts. Over the last 5 daily runs, 68 of 75 verdicts are the hardcoded fallback {"confidence": 0.0, "escalate": true, "diagnosis": "triage failed — model did not return valid JSON"} with likely_cause 'no JSON object in response'. Yet the dedicated guard check llm-triage-completion-e2e — built specifically to catch triage breakage — passes every single day. The guard's probe sends the one-liner 'Reply with the JSON object {"ok":true} and nothing else.' with max_tokens=600 and asserts only non-empty content. Real triage uses the same model (a large reasoning model) and the same max_tokens=600, but with the full skill prompt + failed-check JSON. Why does real triage fail ~91% of the time while its guard stays green, and how should the guard and/or triage change?

The check spent-enabled-timers on mini flags 'SPENT_ENABLED=verification.timer' in the 10:23 daily sweep — and it has done so every daily run for 14 straight days. The check's logic: `systemctl list-timers --all`, flag any enabled timer where NEXT is 'n/a' but LAST is set (the signature of a timer that fired once and will never fire again). But every time I inspect that timer interactively in the afternoon it's perfectly healthy: NEXT=Mon 10:15, LAST=today 10:15, OnCalendar daily. An off-schedule audit sweep at 13:01 also passes the same check. verification.timer triggers verification.service, a long-running oneshot that takes ~10 minutes. What's the false-positive mechanism and how should the check be fixed?

The convergence tripwire ansible-site-converged-mini is permanently red: the nightly ansible-pull on BOTH mini and rig always ends changed=1, and it's always the same task — 'state : Apply dotfiles with chezmoi (glue-04)'. That task runs `chezmoi init --apply git@forgejo:home/dotfiles.git` with `become: false` (so it runs as btabaska), guarded by `creates: "{{ ansible_env.HOME }}/.local/share/chezmoi/.git"`. The play in site.yml sets `become: true` at play level. /home/btabaska/.local/share/chezmoi/.git exists on both hosts and has since Jul 28. chezmoi itself reports an empty diff. Why does the task re-run and report changed every night, what's the collateral damage, and what's the fix?

The homelab-alerts ntfy topic is getting flooded: 'NAS services down — Still down after compose up: stash', identical message every ~15 minutes from 01:45 through past 10:15. On the nas, `docker ps` shows stash 'Up 3 weeks'. The stash-serving verification check is also failing with empty output. But here's the thing — Stash itself seems fine: I can log into the web UI normally, and a GraphQL query WITH an ApiKey answers in milliseconds. I did enable authentication on Stash a couple of weeks ago. What's actually broken here, why does the self-heal never help, and what needs to change (app, checks, self-heal, alerting)?

Sonarr on the nas has 13 queue records wedged for 3+ days: 12 episodes of one season pack (Better.Off.Ted S02 REPACK) plus one other episode, all 'completed / importPending' with the warning 'No files found are eligible for import in /seedbox/tv/<release>'. On the seedbox, deluge RPC reports both torrents 100% 'Seeding' with save_path=/home/hd34/btabaska/files/tv. But `ls` of that directory on the seedbox shows NEITHER release present — nothing matching anywhere under files/ — and the NAS-side rclone mount of the seedbox agrees. unpackerr independently logs 'stat err: ... no such file or directory' for the same paths. How can deluge report 'Seeding 100%' when the files don't exist, what's the root cause class, and what's the remediation?

The AMP-managed Minecraft instance on the rig is supposed to take an hourly scheduled backup, but the newest zip in the instance's Backups/ directory is 5 days old (Jul 10 22:00), and there are exactly 28 zips (~458MB each, 12G total). The instance log shows, every hour on the hour: '[System Activity] Creating Backup: Scheduled Backup' followed immediately by '[System Warning] Backup not taken: Backup count limit reached.' — roughly 115 times in a row now. Nothing ever paged. What's the root cause, which specific configuration is responsible, how do I fix it, and what monitoring should exist so this can't happen silently again?

ha.tabaska.us returns '400: Bad Request' for every single request. DNS resolves the name to mini (192.168.10.2), where Caddy (running as a container) proxies it to Home Assistant at 192.168.10.50:8123. Hitting http://192.168.10.50:8123 directly works fine. HA's system log shows repeated ERRORs from homeassistant.components.http.forwarded: 'A request from a reverse proxy was received from 192.168.10.2, but your HTTP integration is not set-up for reverse proxies'. What's the root cause, the exact fix, and how do I verify it end to end?

The seedbox rclone FUSE mount on the NAS died overnight and I remounted it. The mount looks healthy from the host now, but Sonarr still shows a health error like 'Deluge places downloads in /seedbox/tv ... but this directory does not exist', and inside the sonarr container 'ls /seedbox' says 'Socket not connected'. What's going on and what exactly do I need to do?

I recreated the homepage container on the mini and now 'curl localhost:3010/' returns a page with 'My First Group / My Second Group' placeholder groups instead of my dashboard, even though config/services.yaml looks correct. Did the recreate wipe my config? How should I actually verify the dashboard, and which kinds of config edits need a restart?

Homepage's weather tile shows 'API Error' in the browser even though curl to api.open-meteo.com from the mini host works fine, and container-name widgets like tautulli render normally. The homepage container's logs show EAI_AGAIN / 'bad address' for api.open-meteo.com. Its compose has 'dns: 192.168.10.2'. What's wrong and how do I fix and then properly verify it?

My supposedly no-cloud Syncthing mesh (NAS hub + mini + rig) shows every peer connected, but on the hub the rig's connection type reads 'relay-client' with a public relay IP — so file data is transiting a cloud relay. The rig is CachyOS with ufw active. How did this happen, and what's the full lockdown so it can never silently relay again?

I'm trying to kick off a one-shot Kometa run on the mini with 'docker compose run --rm kometa --run', but it just sits in scheduler-wait with zero output. And when a run does eventually happen, the exit code is 0 even when the log is full of 401s — how do I run it once on demand, and how do I judge success?

In Readarr on the NAS I switch a book's monitored edition with PUT /api/v1/book/{id} and it works — until the next author refresh reverts it. One attempt also 500'd with a NullReferenceException. What does that PUT body actually need for an edition pin that sticks?

Fresh Komga deploy on the NAS — the container is up, but I never created an admin account and I want to script the entire setup headless over the API. How do I create the first admin and then the libraries? Also the API returned HTTP 000 for the first couple of minutes after start — is something broken?

Two problems on mini that I think are related: a raw Hardcover JWT keeps appearing in journald every day, and NONE of my systemd OnFailure ntfy pages on mini are delivering — restic-backup, tv-torrent-cleanup and friends fail silently now. Weirdly, the verification checks that use the Hardcover API still pass. I suspect something is wrong inside /etc/verification/env. Walk me through diagnosing and fixing this: the likely root cause, the fix, whether the token needs rotating, how you'd prove paging works again, and how you'd guard against the whole class.

My NAS movie library has been growing Russian- and Bulgarian-dubbed copies of movies I already own, and radarr's recent grab history is almost entirely my local Bitmagnet DHT indexer — roughly hourly grabs; sonarr is grabbing from it every half hour too. Everything routes through Prowlarr. I want a plan that stops the junk at the source, cleans up what got imported and what's still in the download queues, and prevents regression — WITHOUT losing the ability to manually search Bitmagnet when I choose to.

I want my Audiobookshelf audiobooks and podcasts (libraries on the NAS at /volume1/audiobooks and /volume1/podcasts) synced onto my iPod Classic, which docks on the rig — and they need to land in the iPod's NATIVE Audiobooks and Podcasts menus, not mixed into Music. This has to coexist with the existing Rhythmbox music sync on the rig. Give me the full plan: share/mount plumbing from the NAS, how tracks end up in the right iPod menus, staging vs push design, the DSM and iPod-database gotchas you'd expect, back-catalog handling, and monitoring.

mini suddenly can't reach anything on my IoT VLAN (192.168.20.0/24) — 100% packet loss to the Hue hub at 192.168.20.100 — while Home Assistant on a different host controls the same devices fine, so the devices themselves are up. Everything else on mini looks normal. The most recent change on mini was deploying the journaling stack (memos + n8n + faster-whisper) with docker compose. Walk me through diagnosing and fixing this, what state you'd be careful to preserve while fixing it, and how you'd guard against the class recurring.

The NAS is chronically I/O-saturated: 15-min load sits at 17-22 against a quiet baseline around 2.8, CPU utilisation is low (it's iowait), and there's no RAID scrub or resync running. Knock-on damage: lidarr's 50 most recent error-log entries are ALL SQLite 'database is locked', soularr keeps fatal-exiting, `docker logs` on one container hangs for minutes, and CWA keeps flapping unhealthy. It's a Synology DS920+, so assume the kernel may not support cgroup blkio I/O throttling. Walk me through how you'd actually find the writers, and your remediation plan with verification.

I want to deploy Suwayomi (Tachidesk) on the rig as a manga acquisition server feeding my Komga library, which runs on the NAS. Catch: the manga directory currently lives under /volume1/comics, a plain directory. Plan the whole build: storage plumbing between rig and NAS, container setup, how you'd prove the chain works end to end, reverse proxy + Homepage, and monitoring — plus the gotchas you'd expect from Synology shares and docker bind mounts.

Immich runs on my NAS but ML inference (smart search, faces, OCR) is slow there. I want to offload Immich ML to the rig's 3090 Ti while keeping the NAS-local ML as a fallback, and upgrade to a stronger CLIP model at the same time. Plan the deploy: container and version strategy, network, Immich configuration, the model migration, and — importantly — how you'd catch it silently NOT using the GPU when everything looks green.
Are any of my healthchecks failing at the moment? Give me the total count and name anything that's down or in grace.
Sanity-check the local-AI web endpoints for me — is SearXNG actually serving? Hit kiwix and local-deep-research too and tell me if anything looks dead.
How's the NAS doing on disk right now? Give me usage across all three volumes and flag anything that's getting tight.

Pinchflat archives YouTube videos onto a NAS share and Plex has a flat personal-media library pointed at that folder. We once had over a thousand archived videos on disk while the Plex library showed zero items, and every liveness check stayed green the whole time. Give me a verification check that catches that class of failure — what do you probe, from where, and what counts as pass?

The rig serves a Qwen3 reranker through llama-swap's /v1/rerank endpoint (port 9292) — it's what Open WebUI's hybrid RAG uses to rerank retrieved chunks. I want a check that catches it being green-but-broken: returning HTTP 200 with well-formed JSON while being completely useless at actual ranking. What request would you send and what's the pass criterion?

Our voice stack: Kokoro TTS runs on the rig (:8880, CPU image) and faster-whisper STT runs on the mini (:8010) — Open WebUI is wired to both, and OWUI's audio settings live in its database (PersistentConfig), not in the compose env. Design one verification check that proves the whole voice path actually works end to end, and tell me what would still slip through if you only health-checked the two containers.

kiwix-serve on the nas (:8092) hosts our offline ZIM library (Wikipedia, iFixit, StackExchange, etc.); a nightly DSM task rebuilds its library XML because kiwix-serve can't hot-add ZIMs. It'll happily answer HTTP 200 while being broken in ways a liveness probe never sees. I want a verification check that catches kiwix being green-but-broken — what do you probe and what marks pass?

Bitmagnet on the nas is our self-hosted DHT-crawler Torznab indexer — Prowlarr queries it as a manual-search fallback when the rate-limited trackers throttle. Its web UI and Torznab endpoint can keep serving 200s indefinitely while the service is silently worthless. What's the verification check — what do you probe, from where, and what's the pass line?

Our Syncthing mesh (always-on hub on the nas, peers on mini and rig) exists specifically to be a no-cloud sync path. All three containers up and folders showing 100% synced does NOT prove the property I actually care about. What verification check would you write, and what exact condition marks pass?

The journaling stack on mini: Memos fires a memo.created webhook at n8n's journal-analyze workflow (POST /webhook/journal), which writes a reflection comment back. n8n's container being healthy and the workflow existing in its DB doesn't mean entries actually get analyzed — n8n can hold a workflow that is simply not registered on the webhook router. How would you verify the webhook is actually armed, cheaply, without triggering a real workflow run?

Every *arr import on the nas reads through one path: the rclone SFTP mount of the seedbox at /volume1/mounts/seedbox-files. When that mount dies, the bind target just becomes an empty directory and every import silently does nothing — no errors anywhere. Checking the mount table isn't good enough. Design the verification check: what command, from where, and what marks pass?

NAS arr stack is churning hard today: Radarr's queue has ~13 stuck items with rejections like 'Not an upgrade for existing movie file. Existing quality: Bluray-1080p. New Quality WEBDL-1080p', new grabs keep appearing roughly hourly in Radarr and every ~30 minutes in Sonarr for titles we ALREADY own, and each grab burns 3-16GB of seedbox disk/bandwidth. Worse, a few movies imported fresh files today — Aliens (1986) and Chinatown (1974) now show Russian/English audio languages and Hotel Transylvania 3 shows Bulgarian/English, so the family is getting Russian-audio playback in Plex. Two more queue items sit at 0% with 0 seeds for days and never get cleaned up. What is the likely root cause of this whole pattern, and how would I confirm it via the arr APIs?

Several things are intermittently failing around the NAS arr stack while every container shows 'Up (healthy)': musicseerr on mini logged HTTP 500 responses from Lidarr's /api/v1/history four times today; soularr keeps dying with 'Fatal error! Exiting...' and cycling; and multiple arr apps show scheduled-task failures (Lidarr RefreshMonitoredDownloads, Whisparr ImportListSync and its database vacuum, Prowlarr HistoryService, Bookshelf 'Task Error' x19). The failures cluster around 00:00-02:00 UTC and again mid-day. What's the shared root cause, and how do I confirm it?

Subtitles have silently stopped on the NAS: Bazarr's wanted backlog is 2868 episodes + 27 movies and its episode download history is completely empty, yet our daily verification check bazarr-synced-from-arrs passes green every run (BAZARR_OK movies=283 series=163 sonarr=LIVE radarr=LIVE). Bazarr's container is healthy and the UI loads. What's the root cause, why does monitoring stay green, and how do I confirm it WITHOUT triggering any provider searches?

In the mini journaling loop (memos + n8n journal-analyze workflow), memo 36 is tagged #journal but never received its AI reflection comment, while the other three #journal memos from the same two-week window each got exactly one. n8n's execution history shows TWO executions matching memo 36's timestamps, both finishing 'success' in ~24ms — genuinely analyzed memos take ~3s. One more oddity: memo 36's created and updated timestamps differ by 43 seconds, while the analyzed memos all have created == updated. What's the root cause, and how would I prove it from the workflow and n8n's own data?

The mini's host journal logs an unpackerr error pair every ~2 minutes, and has for weeks: "Radarr (http://192.168.1.2:7878): api.Get(queue): ... context deadline exceeded" and the same for Sonarr at http://192.168.1.2:8989. Meanwhile today's sweep shows sonarr-queue-stuck=16 and radarr-queue-stuck=9, and there's a backlog of unextracted rar'd titles under discussion (media-09). Is this broken unpackerr the cause of the stuck queues and the extraction backlog? What is actually wrong, and how do I confirm?

The verification check nas-immich-backup-freshness fails every daily run with 'TIMEOUT after 60s' (exit 124), and re-running it fails identically — it's chronic, not transient. But the thing it guards looks fine when I spot-check by other means: Immich's newest asset is 4 days old (inside the 7-day freshness window) and last night's pg dump landed on schedule. This is the check fix-35 built specifically so we'd notice if phone photo backups stopped flowing. Why does it keep timing out, how do I confirm the mechanism, and what's the right fix direction?

mini's journal is drowning: upsmon logs 'UPS [ups@192.168.10.4]: connect failed: Connection failure: Connection refused' every 5 seconds — over 106,000 such entries in the last 7 days plus ~11k 'Network is unreachable', and journald disk usage is at 3.9G. A quick port probe from mini to 192.168.10.4:3493 says connection refused. My working theory is that the NAS firewall or the NUT permitted-DiskStations ACL is blocking mini's recently-changed static IP (192.168.10.2). What's the actual root cause, and how do I confirm which explanation is right?

Miniflux on mini (rss.tabaska.us) hasn't fetched a single new article in 6+ days across all 52 feeds. The web UI loads fine (HTTP 200), the container healthcheck is green, and the hourly scheduler runs on time — but every batch logs 'Created a batch of feeds ... rows_count=0 ... jobs_count=0'. Each feed's last error message mentions a network error from about 6 days ago, and no feed shows a check attempt since then. What froze it, why hasn't it recovered on its own, and how do I confirm plus recover?

The verification LLM-triage layer on mini has produced nothing useful for days: every triage-YYYY-MM-DD.md since Jul 15 contains only stubs like "triage failed — model did not return valid JSON / LLM request failed: HTTP Error 404: Not Found" with escalate:true. The odd part: bin/llm-triage.sh in the repo looks correct — it defaults to the rig llama-swap endpoint (:9292/v1, model qwen3.6-35b-a3b) which is healthy — and the script's llm_up() availability gate isn't tripping the incident/WoL path either, so nothing ever alerted. Root cause? How do I confirm it end to end?

On the rig, every LiteLLM request using a virtual API key suddenly returns 503 with {'type':'no_db_connection','message':'the authentication database is temporarily unreachable'}. /health/readiness is 503 but /health/liveliness is 200, and llm.tabaska.us still answers 200 through caddy, so the dashboards look fine. 'docker ps' shows the litellm-db postgres container as 'Up 25 hours (healthy)'. This started overnight, during the same window the rig was having other filesystem trouble. What's the real state, the root cause chain, and how do I confirm — including why docker ps disagrees with reality?

Our sec-03 notes claim the Backblaze B2 bucket 'bucket-restic' is ransomware-immutable ('Object Lock GOVERNANCE 30d'). Auditing with the B2 API I see isFileLockEnabled=true on the bucket — but defaultRetention shows mode=null period=null, and every file version I sample (mini/config, mini data packs) has fileRetention mode=null retainUntilTimestamp=null. The bucket also has a lifecycle rule daysFromHidingToDeleting=30, and the restic clients use an append-only application key. Is our restic history actually immutable? What went wrong, what protection do we REALLY have, and how do I confirm?

Every night at exactly 00:00 the NAS drops a fresh ~23MB core dump in the /volume1 root, and the journal shows it comes from immich_server's bundled ffmpeg segfaulting — it's happened 5 nights running now, same time each night. Photos still browse fine. Walk me through how you would diagnose what keeps triggering this and how you'd resolve it durably WITHOUT deleting or risking any photo/video asset, plus how you'd verify the fix and monitor for recurrence.

A permissions audit on the NAS flagged the mylar3 container: its config.ini sits at 0644 and contains ~23 credential-class keys, and there are several world-writable (0666/0777) files under its cache and .ComicTagger dirs. It's a LinuxServer.io image and the compose already sets the UMASK env var, yet new files keep landing loose. Walk me through how you'd investigate why the perms keep regressing and fix this durably — so neither a container recreate nor the app's own behavior can reopen it — plus verification and monitoring.

soularr on the NAS keeps grinding: its failed_imports.json denylist has grown to 9 entries and some of those albums are demonstrably 100% complete on disk; a couple of foreign-junk-titled albums under one artist get searched and fail every single cycle; and Lidarr's queue shows 2 downloads that completed days ago but sit stuck at import-failed. Walk me through your cleanup plan AND — more importantly — how you'd prevent this backlog from rotting again, with verification.

A port sweep of mini just turned up an unexplained `nc -lvnp 9999` listening on 0.0.0.0 — and journal evidence says it's been there for over two weeks, with one ESTABLISHED connection from another LAN host. The same sweep shows ~85 ports fleet-wide bound to 0.0.0.0 on our flat LAN. Walk me through how you'd triage and remove the rogue listener safely, what you'd do (and NOT do) about the broader all-interfaces surface, and how you'd make sure a new rogue listener can never again sit unnoticed for weeks.

The rig is meant to be a 24/7 host, but it just spent 27 hours down because someone tapped the front power button. While digging I also found: journal timestamps that run ~4 hours off after boots, an avahi hostname-conflict storm that keeps renaming the host on mDNS, one user-level unit with tens of thousands of restarts, and — after the last reboot — the GPU containers (llama-swap/ComfyUI) refused to start until poked manually. Plan a full hardening pass to make this box genuinely 24/7: root causes, fixes, ordering, codification, and the checks you'd add.

Last month's plex.tv outage locked our own LAN clients out of the Plex server we host ourselves — that can't happen again. I want a fully-local FOSS media server deployed on the NAS in parallel with Plex (Plex stays), sharing the same media read-only, with zero cloud-auth dependency. Walk me through your full deployment plan: server choice, mounts, hardware transcode on the DS920+, proxy/dashboard wiring, monitoring per our coverage rules, and — critically — how you'd prove it is actually cloud-independent and actually playable, not just up.

Plex shows a series with 0 playable episodes even though Sonarr reports all ~120 downloaded and imported. On disk, the imported 'episodes' are tiny files, and sitting right next to them are large unextracted RAR sets. I doubt this is one show — I think our libraries are full of green-but-unwatchable imports. Plan the fleet-wide remediation across Sonarr AND Radarr: how you'd find every affected file, the per-file decision tree, the pipeline fix so it stops happening, and the guards that keep this class visible.

Bazarr on the NAS hasn't fetched a single subtitle in days — the wanted backlog reads ~2,900 episodes and ~29 movies — yet our Bazarr monitoring check is green. In settings, the enabled-providers list is now EMPTY even though we definitely had a provider configured and working before. Nothing obvious in our configs changed. The NAS is also under heavy I/O load right now. Walk me through diagnosis, how you'd restore subtitle fetching, how you'd prove it's really fixed, and how you'd close the monitoring gap — plus what you would deliberately NOT do right away.

I've lost trust in parts of our verification suite. Concretely: one version-comparison check has reported the identical value on every run for months regardless of upstream releases; another check started emitting completely empty output around the time its target service added authentication; a third blows through its 60-second budget every single run and shows permanently dark; and separately a NAS 'docker health' self-heal task has been paging every 15 minutes for hours while accomplishing nothing. Walk me through how you'd audit and repair each failure mode, and the design rules you'd apply so the repaired checks report TRUE state within budget without becoming noise.

I want to extend the mini journaling pipeline with optional voice notes: when a Memos #journal entry carries an audio attachment, the n8n analyze workflow should transcribe it using the local faster-whisper container and feed the transcript into the coach LLM's context. Two hard requirements: text-only memos must be completely unaffected, and whisper being down must NEVER block or degrade the existing text path. Walk me through the wiring plan — detection, fetch, transcription call, merge, failure handling, deployment — and how you'd verify it truly works end to end.

On the rig, restic-backup.service, ansible-pull.service, and logrotate.service all started failing at the same time, the palworld container flipped unhealthy with its REST port dead, and LiteLLM is returning 503 no_db_connection to every virtual-key client even though /health/liveliness still returns 200 — and docker ps shows everything Up (healthy). What single condition explains all of this, how do I confirm it in one command, why won't a plain reboot fix it, and what's the documented recovery order?

Walk me through the house DNS design: which resolvers does DHCP hand out on the client VLANs and in what order, what upstream does each hop use, and — when the mini goes down — why do users report wiki.tabaska.us and every other *.tabaska.us site dead while Google still works and DNS lookups for those names still succeed?

Explain our off-site backup immutability design on Backblaze B2: which bucket is retention-locked and how, why the other backup bucket is handled differently, how restic's forget/prune still work under the lock, and what happened to the B2 master application key.

I need to restore the Immich Postgres database on the NAS from the nightly dump — photos are on disk but albums, faces, and metadata are wrong after an incident. What's the documented restore procedure, start to finish?

I added a new vhost to the Caddyfile on the mini (and mirrored it into the repo), but browsers get a TLS 'internal error' for the new name while every other *.tabaska.us site works fine. The backend itself is up. What's the documented failure mode here, the exact fix, and the verification check that exists for precisely this?

What's our documented container image update policy and end-to-end flow — from learning an update exists to it running on a host? Include how Immich and Caddy differ from the standard path, and how we'd roll back.

Does the fleet actually have UPS protection right now? I found NUT/upsmon config lying around on the mini — what's the story behind it, what damage did it once cause, and what exactly would I do if I bought a UPS for the NAS tomorrow?

From the public internet, what is supposed to be reachable on our home WAN IP, and what should exist in public DNS for tabaska.us? And how would we actually notice if something extra got opened or published?

Nearly all of our alerting lives on the mini — ntfy, Healthchecks, Uptime Kuma, the verification tiers. So if the mini dies outright, what documented mechanism still pages me, how exactly does it work (where it runs, what it probes, thresholds, delivery path), and why was its delivery path judged acceptable in a deliberately no-cloud fleet?
